overview: Black answers the Polish with a King's Indian fianchetto, ...Nf6, ...g6, ...Bg7 and ...d6. White usually plays 3.c4 Bg7 4.e3 d6 5.Nf3 O-O, with the b2 bishop on the long diagonal and queenside space, or the sharper Spike and Schiffler tries with g4 or e4. Play is flank-oriented, with unbalanced pawn structures and no early forcing theory.

white_ideas.idea: Use the b2 bishop on the long diagonal and gain queenside space
Build with c4, e3 and Nf3, then d4 or a4-b5
Spike with g4 or e4 for a surprise attack

black_ideas.idea: Fianchetto and challenge the long diagonal with ...Bg7
Strike in the centre with ...d5 or ...e5
Aim at the advanced b4 pawn with ...a5 or ...c5

typical_structures.structure: Flank structure with White b4/c4 and a b2 bishop against a Black kingside fianchetto

character.notes: Flank play with unbalanced structures but little early forcing play.

approach.notes: Played rarely by strong players, mainly as a surprise.
